rounds.text: Conceded: [E13], [E14]. Despite reported historical growth, the company suffers from a severe cash flow collapse, registering a negative operating cash flow of Rs -350 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -373 Cr in Mar 2026 [E22, E23]. This creates an alarming cash conversion ratio of -7.78x against reported profit, meaning operating cash flow represents -402% of operating profit [E21, E24]. This cash drain has forced a sudden and massive accumulation of debt, with borrowings surging to Rs 278 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 0 Cr just a year prior [E27]. Consequently, the debt-to-equity ratio has deteriorated to 1.70x, meaning debt now exceeds the company's net worth and introduces substantial financial risk [E25]. Furthermore, insiders are quietly reducing their stake, with promoters trimming holdings from 74.30% in Sep 2023 to 71.15% in Jun 2026 [E29]. Investors must also reckon with extreme historical volatility and vulnerability, evidenced by a catastrophic worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -87.4% and a complete lack of shareholder return through dividends at 0.00% yield [E4, E39].

Conceded: [E22, E23, E27]. While borrowings rose to Rs 278 Cr alongside negative operating and free cash flows [E22, E23, E27], the company's fundamental earning power and operational expansion remain exceptionally strong, with 5-year sales and profit growth at 178% and 133% respectively [E13, E14], alongside a stellar rules-based screen score of 91 out of 100 [E44]. Conceded: [E29]. Although promoter holdings saw a minor reduction to 71.15% [E29], institutional flow reads neutral [E30] and management continues to deliver expanding operating margins, which reached 14% in June 2026 compared to 6% in the prior-year quarter [E18]. Conceded: [E39]. Despite historical drawdowns [E39], the stock exhibits robust current momentum with a 12-month return of 101.1% [E38], a high Sharpe ratio of 1.95 [E41], and a relative-strength rating of 92 against the Nifty 500 [E37]. Furthermore, the lack of dividend yield [E4] is irrelevant to the core undervaluation thesis, given that a reverse DCF shows the current market price implies an unrealistic -12.1% earnings growth rate [E33] while trading at an extremely attractive P/E of 5.75x [E1] compared to a sector benchmark of 35.78x [E6].

Conceded: [E13, E14, E44]. While multi-year growth and rules-based screening scores look impressive on paper, they completely ignore the catastrophic collapse in liquidity where operating cash flow plunged to negative Rs 350 Cr and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 373 Cr in March 2026 [E22, E23]. The bull's reliance on a low P/E multiple of 5.75x [E1] masks a dangerous build-up of debt, with borrowings shooting from zero to Rs 278 Cr in a single year, pushing the debt-to-equity ratio to a precarious 1.70x where debt exceeds net worth [E25, E27]. Conceded: [E18]. Although operating margins expanded in the June 2026 quarter [E18], the quarterly margin trend is officially flagged as inconsistent [E20], and cash conversion has cratered to a staggering -7.78x against reported profit [E21]. Furthermore, promoters have quietly trimmed their stake to 71.15% [E29], and investors face a complete lack of income with a 0.00% dividend yield [E4].
